message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV (first) |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV (negative, meaning it does not readily accept an electron) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Atomic radius | ~31 pm (covalent) |
| | Van der Waals radius | ~120 pm |
| | Density (at 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ (lightest element) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (−423.17 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (−434.69 °F) |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas at 0 °C, 1 atm) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat capacity (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 298 K) |
| | Thermal conductivity | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ (at 300 K) |
| | Specific heat ratio (γ) | 1.41 (diatomic gas) |
| | Speed of sound in H₂ | ~1275 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| **Physical State & Behavior** | State at STP | Diatomic gas (H₂) |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Slightly soluble in many (e.g., ethanol, acetone) |
| | Flame color | Pale blue (non-luminous) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic, ΔH ≈ –286 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Oxidation states | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as hydride H⁻) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a proton donor (H⁺) in aqueous solution |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydride ions (H⁻) in metal hydrides |
| | Redox behavior | Easily oxidized to H⁺; reduced to H₂ under suitable conditions |
| | Bonding | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic H₂ is a single σ bond |
| | Spectroscopy | Strong absorption in UV (Lyman series) and infrared (vibrational transitions) |
| | Isotopic effects | Deuterium and tritium form heavier isotopologues with slightly different vibrational frequencies and boiling/melting points |
| **Astrophysical & Industrial Relevance** | Stellar fusion | Proton–proton chain (H → He) powers the Sun |
| | Fusion fuel | Deuterium–tritium (D–T) fusion in experimental reactors |
| | Energy storage | Hydrogen fuel cells (electrochemical conversion to electricity) |
| | Rocket propellant | Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) used with liquid oxygen (LOX) |
| | Chemical industry | Feedstock for ammonia (NH₃), methanol (CH₃OH), and many other chemicals |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (water vapor) but requires renewable energy for green hydrogen production |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe.
- **Diatomic gas**: At room temperature and pressure, it exists as H₂ molecules.
- **Highly reactive**: It readily forms both acids (as H⁺) and bases (as H⁻) and participates in a wide range of chemical reactions.
- **Energy carrier**: Hydrogen is a promising clean energy vector, especially when produced via electrolysis powered by renewable sources.
- **Astrophysical importance**: It fuels stellar fusion and is central to the chemistry of the cosmos.

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
